newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to end S.African ostrich meat ban.
newsitem.headline: EU to end S.African ostrich meat ban.

text.p: The European Union is set to agree later this month a conditional end to a ban on imports of South African ostrich meat, European Commission officials said on Thursday.
The EU banned imports in November after an outbreak of Congo-Crimean haemorrhagic fever, a deadly viral disease destroying body organs and causing massive internal bleeding.
"A proposal could be adopted by the Commission in a couple of weeks," an official said. Senior EU veterinary scientists supported the move on Wednesday after examining new South African research.
The research showed that contaminated ostrich meat carried the risk of infection for only five days.
The EU ban would be lifted on condition that ostriches were either kept in quarantine for two weeks before slaughter or ostrich meat was quarantined for two weeks after slaughter.
Ostrich meat has become more popular in Europe in recent years, due partly to health fears about possible infection from beef contaminated with mad cow disease.
